html:
The Yeopim were a small Algonquian-speaking people of northeastern North Carolina, on the north shore of Albemarle Sound. English records of the 1580s, from the time of the Roanoke colonies, call the people of this area the Weapemeoc; later colonists knew them as the Yeopim.

They lived in farming and fishing villages along the sounds, like the Pamlico to the south. English settlers moved into the Albemarle region from Virginia in the mid 1600s, and the Yeopim sold land to them. Disease and settlement cut their numbers, and by the 1700s only a few families remained, some of them living near the Tuscarora and other Native communities.
